hypothesis: The measured 32-column local-accumulator tile was valid but much slower (0.047509 s) than row-parallel r-k-c without SIMD (0.009477 s); the cause is not established. Test whether reducing the tile to eight columns makes local accumulation and SIMD more effective while retaining ascending-k order and caller-capped row parallelism. Each C element is written once, so a separate output memset is unnecessary. No speedup is assumed.
notes: The 8-column tile covers arbitrary positive n with a short final tile. Accumulators start at zero and each output element receives contributions in ascending k order; every output element is assigned on each positive-size call. Row parallelism remains capped by min(threads,n), with a serial path for a nonpositive or single-thread budget. The controller should verify overwrite behavior, oracle tolerance on all official sizes, and repeated native n=1024 timings; no measurement is claimed here.
transformations: Use an eight-element local accumulator for each output-column tile; traverse k in ascending order and SIMD-update the contiguous B segment for each tile.
Write each output element once after its tile accumulation, eliminating the separate output memset while preserving full overwrite behavior.
Retain static row-parallel execution capped by min(threads,n), with a serial path when the cap is at most one.
